content.text: tetany: calcium gluconate 10 mL of 10% solution IV over 10 min; response can be dramatic but may last only a few hours; may need repeat boluses or 20 to 30 mL of 10% calcium gluconate in 1 L D5W over 12 to 24 h; hazardous w digoxin: give slowly w continuous ECG monitoring after checking for (and correcting) hypokalemia.
Calcium gluconate in NaCl injection dose, acute symptomatic hypocalcemia (adults):

Adults: initial dose 1,000 mg to 2,000 mg. Subsequent doses 1,000 mg to 2,000 mg every 6 h if needed. Continuous infusion: initiate at 5.4 mg/kg/h to 21.5 mg/kg/h. Bolus rate: ⍉ exceed 200 mg/min in adults.
Calcium gluconate in NaCl injection safety:

CI: hypercalcemia. CI: neonates (28 days of age or younger) receiving ceftriaxone. Avoid in pts receiving cardiac glycosides; if necessary, give slowly in small amounts w/ close ECG monitoring. ⍉ give ceftriaxone simultaneously w/ calcium via a Y-site in any age group. Calcinosis cutis can occur w/ or w/o extravasation; tissue necrosis, ulceration, and secondary infection are the most serious complications. If extravasation or calcinosis cutis signs occur, stop IV at that site immediately and treat as needed. Rapid injection may cause vasodilation, ↓BP, bradycardia, arrhythmias, syncope, and cardiac arrest; infuse slowly. Measure serum Ca every 4 to 6 h during intermittent infusions and every 1 to 4 h during continuous infusion. OD may cause hypercalcemia; symptoms typically develop when total serum Ca is ≥12 mg/dL. If OD occurs, stop administration immediately and give supportive tx to restore intravascular volume and promote urinary Ca excretion if needed.
